  "title": "twitter.com returns 902 when strict mode on FF",
  "body": "https://twitter.com/ returns '902' http code when I use Strict mode on Firefox 65.0. Why? and I was wondering if you could get rid of these errors. Thanks.\r\n![error](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30253227/52310004-34b46d00-29e5-11e9-9e8b-51754f422e42.png)\r\n![options](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30253227/52310008-3847f400-29e5-11e9-84c9-9887e209d0c7.png)\r\n",

      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Hi,\r\n\r\nthat's because twitter.com is a \"known tracker\" and \"known trackers\" are blocked with your strict settings. There is no way around the tracking protection for WebExtensions. From Bookmarks Organizer's point of view there are two options:\r\n\r\na) Bookmarks Organizer could control the tracking protection. But I am not sure if it should because only one add-on can control the tracking protection and I don't think a bookmarks extension should do this.\r\n\r\nb) Bookmarks Organizer should add a sentence that there will be more false positives with tracking protection enabled.\r\n\r\nIt's not yet decided but I think b) will the way to go. If a) will be implemented, then it's a duplicate of #77."
    }
